resources.string: Backups protect the business if the phone is lost. %1$s keeps nothing of its own: each person picks their cloud.
%1$s hands each backup to the cloud already on the phone, and that cloud uploads it when it can. %1$s cannot tell if it arrived: it requires checking the cloud every week.
%1$s cannot hand backups to that cloud on its own. Each one is handed over by hand, with the app open, and it requires checking the cloud every week.
%1$s uploads each backup and checks that it arrived. It requires opening an account with another service and entering its address, user name and password here.
One backup per day for the last week, with photos.
Other clouds have not been tested for this option. If they offer WebDAV, they connect with Service with WebDAV. If not, Local backups remain, on a card or a USB drive.

Each backup holds all the business data, including customers. Each person chooses the service, and %1$s does not run it. Without encryption, that service can read the backups, and encryption can be turned on. Without backups, the data is only on this phone.

%1$s cannot tell whether that cloud uploaded each backup. If it fails silently and the phone is lost, everything recorded after the last backup that truly uploaded is lost: about 7 days or more. It only comes to light when checking.
That is why the file\'s time must be checked in the cloud every week, ideally from another device, and confirmed in %1$s.
